steps.content: With a soft thud, you close the folder containing Dove's file and related information. The preliminary investigation has yielded so little information that you feel like you've read nothing at all.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I guess that's normal... Information on Outland Sinners has always been hard to come by. Looks like I'll have to wait for tomorrow's interrogation to learn more about her.
You set the reviewed documents aside, rubbing your fingertips together.
The flimsy file mirrors Dove herself. An innocent facade that somehow feels elusive and even a little off.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Yes, I am a Sinner, and yes, I forged the letters. Maybe you see that as an unforgivable crime...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: But I really don't know anything about the Mania or any truth of this town! I have my own reasons for doing all this!
Reasons... You've heard all kinds of pretty excuses from people who wanted to justify their actions. You won't be fooled easily by her crude attempt at explaining away her deeds.
And yet... something about her tear-filled eyes lingers in your memory, leaving you with the nagging feeling that the pain glimpsed beneath the surface isn't entirely an act.
Could there really be some unknown motive behind her series of cruel deceptions in the town? Something you've yet to uncover?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Excuse me, Chief. We've just received a visit request for Sinner Dove.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Like the previous times... we need your response as soon as possible.
Nightingale's telling hesitation gives you a good idea of what to expect.
Taking the visit request form, you glance at it and find exactly what you expected. You can't help but let out a weary sigh.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...The same person? I'll give him credit for being persistent.
You're too familiar with the name on the request form by now. The background check shows that he's a merchant who brokers deals between DisCity and Outlands and often travels in WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I hear he's been bragging at dinner parties about having found a new gold mine? Well, at least he knew better than to state his true purpose on the visit request.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Disasters and storms are common in WhiteSands, making regular electronic communication equipment highly vulnerable to damage. High-end devices are only affordable for the wealthy, so most people still rely on the old way to communicate: by mail.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: He wants to exploit this situation by using a Sinner's abilities to forge letters and scam people... Should I call that gutsy or just shameless?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Sinner Dove's condition is stable and her special power is low-risk. And considering that her previous offenses didn't result in any serious harm, she's likely to be granted bail or at least permission to leave the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The man must have noticed this and sees her as a money-making tool he can manipulate. That's why he wants to establish contact with Dove early, so he can put her to work the moment she's released on bail.
While Nightingale's deduction seems sound, you shake your head.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If this was truly just one merchant's scheme, it would be simple enough. We can just decline the request. But why would a mere merchant happen to know the exact details of a Sinner's special power...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And how convenient that this visit request, which normally requires multiple levels of internal approval, lands on my desk the day before her interrogation? Not to mention how brazenly he's advertising his intentions.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: You mean to say... DisCity's higher-ups are involved, and this scheme to exploit a Sinner's powers for profit isn't just some merchant's random idea?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I understand now. I'll handle it appropriately. Would you like me to reschedule Dove's interrogation tomorrow?
You look at the visit request and Dove's file laid side by side before you, pause for a moment to think, then reach out to pile them into a single stack.
No doubt, this business plan isn't just illegal but is also morally reprehensible. Under normal circumstances, no amount of pressure could make you complicit in such corruption.

But this man has appeared at an almost perfect timing. His plausible yet sinister scheme bears some unexpected resemblance to Dove's own actions in Désir. Perhaps it could serve as a touchstone to reveal her true nature.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No need to change it. We'll proceed with the interrogation tomorrow as scheduled.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: It's been a while, ${PlayerName}. You look so much more commanding than you did in Désir, and way cooler too... I almost didn't recognize you!
The girl taps the toes of her shoes against the floor and smiles modestly, her ever-present messenger bag resting on her knees pressed demurely together.

Truth be told, the farewell between you two in Désir was far from pleasant, which makes her current composure and friendliness seem oddly suspicious, like a carefully laid trap waiting for you to slip in.
But you're no longer the green interrogator you once were. In response to her calculated move, you reply calmly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's been a while, Dove. You... don't seem much different. I take it you're adjusting well to life at the Bureau?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Well... life in DisCity has turned out quite different than what I expected. It took some getting used to at first, but everyone's been so warm and kind to me. Thanks to them, I've really settled in.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's good to hear. As it happens, I've just received a routine report from the Drifter Camp. It seems like the other folks from Désir are starting to settle in as well.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The authorities have provided basic necessities, but they need to be self-sufficient to truly survive. It also helps them break free from the false dreams certain individuals had once woven for them.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Drifter... Camp...? I didn't know such a place existed in DisCity. Though I'm not sure what it's like there, if you say so, ${PlayerName}, I can finally put my mind at ease.
Dove keeps her head tilted as she listens intently, and even as you make those pointed remarks, she merely pats her chest to show her relief.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: As they say in the books, each new day brings a fresh start, and everything will get better. I believe that as long as everyone stays grounded, they'll find happiness. I'll be cheering for them here in the Bureau too!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Well, I've heard that while some people demanded to return to Désir and wanted their old lifestyle back at first, quite a few have found jobs now. They're truly making a fresh start.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: That's wonderful! Everyone is so resilient and brave! As for those who are still reluctant... ${PlayerName}, could you give them more time? I believe they're not weak. They're just still processing everything.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Even I sometimes think back to my days as a mail carrier in Désir... After all, it was our shared home filled with so many wonderful memories together. ${PlayerName}, please be more patient with them, will you?

Her optimistic outlook and sincere concern reveal no cracks despite your probing words. To any observer, she would appear to be nothing more than a kind-hearted girl who gives everyone her unreserved support.
...Or rather, she's very good at playing such a character. Even though she knows you've seen her hidden side before, she's confident she can keep up the act. In that case...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you miss your days as a mail carrier in Désir? Even though Désir didn't have too many residents, constantly going back and forth delivering mail must have been quite demanding.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Looks like being a mail carrier gave you quite a sense of accomplishment. Is that why you can't seem to let it go?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Heh, ${PlayerName}, you've got that right. Though if I have to go into more detail, we may get sidetracked...

Your more direct question has been deflected effortlessly. The atmosphere shifts subtly yet suddenly, as if someone is gently tightening the very trap you've stepped in, snickering at the capture of their prey.
Dove's smile fades as her voice grows soft and slow, as if preparing to tell you a tale from long ago.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Actually, my parents were mail carriers too. Ever since I was little, I watched them work tirelessly delivering mail for everyone back in our hometown.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I was born far from DisCity, in a remote village. Back home, resources were scarce and everyone was poor. We were constantly plagued by all sorts of disasters.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Even basic survival depended on messengers like my parents, who kept communication flowing throughout the community... As for me, being a sickly child, I was mostly confined to our home.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Sounds kinda sad, doesn't it? But I never felt that way at all! My parents would bring back books and stories from the outside world, so I could explore it myself through text, even when I couldn't leave home.
She straightens her posture and meets your gaze, her eyes showing just the right amount of determination.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: They taught me that mail could spread knowledge and communicate human emotions. It carries thoughts and hopes, connecting separated souls, villages, and cities across vast distances.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Being a mail carrier is a noble calling. That's why I always dreamed of becoming one just like my parents.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: E-even though delivering mail meant facing countless dangers, even attacks from monsters...
She lowers her head, her body and voice trembling slightly as if recalling the pain once inflicted upon her.

According to the infirmary's report, the Mania contamination in Dove's body does match the characteristics of a Corruptor infection. So far, she doesn't seem to be lying, but this only makes that weird sense of inconsistency you feel from her even more inexplicable.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can see being a mail carrier means a great deal to you. Actually, what I wanted to discuss today is related to your work...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Someone wants to bail you out and hire you as a mail carrier on the Outland routes... You'd be happy to accept the offer, wouldn't you?
You nod with feigned understanding, casually mentioning the merchant's visit as bait while carefully observing Dove's reaction.
Sure enough, Dove's dejected expression instantly vanishes, her pupils dilating with joy as if what she's just heard is too good to be true.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...Really? Can I? Yes, of course I'd love to accept it! I'll work hard to be a good mail carrier and deliver letters to everyone, just like I did in Désir!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: This is what I learned from my parents! They passed this noble calling on to me, and I won't let them down!
Her eyes sparkle with anticipation as she instinctively clutches her messenger bag. Her words overflow with genuine admiration and respect for both her parents and the profession.

In Désir, she was equally inseparable from her messenger bag, which you know was filled with intercepted letters she opened without permission. They were both evidence of her forgeries and a symbol of the trust she betrayed.
Indeed, Dove's enthusiasm seems genuine, as does her devotion to letters, and that's precisely what contradicts her actions in Désir. Unless... A theory begins to form in your mind.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You seem so excited. I wonder if it's because you can return to your profession and fulfill your noble calling... or because you can go back to deceiving more people with forged letters?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...I knew it. Even if you didn't bring it up at first, you still remember what happened. You still think I'm just a dishonest, bad person.
Dove flinches at your pointed question, but quickly straightens up and meets your gaze with determined resolve.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: But... back then in Désir, I truly didn't know what else I could do. I just wanted to protect everyone's feelings from the cruel reality...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I know what I did might be wrong, but I was just trying to do what my parents taught me, to help everyone live better lives by delivering heartfelt messages. If I have to pay the price for that... then so be it.
In the interrogation room, her desperate defense trails off into a heavy silence charged with emotion. The girl lowers her gaze hopelessly, waiting quietly for your response.
But unfortunately for her, you won't give her the sympathy and leniency she's fishing for.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Dove, the very act of forging letters contradicts your claims about a mail carrier's duty of delivering heartfelt messages. No amount of glorification will change that fact.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I think... you've told me all this just to win my sympathy and absolve yourself of your crimes.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: No, that's not it... I'm not lying, I swear I'm not!
As if shocked by your ruthless words, Dove's face crumples with hurt as her eyes instantly well up with tears, glistening in the light.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Just now, you described Désir's situation as the cruel reality, which shows you were somewhat aware of the truth behind, or at the very least, you knew its condition was deteriorating.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But you didn't expose the truth to give the others a chance to escape, nor did you follow Vautour Bleu's example of believing in and protecting this illusion until the very end...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You were simply being a bystander who took no active action. Don't you see how that contradicts the image you've been trying to craft for yourself: someone sincere, kind, and strong?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: No, you're wrong! ${PlayerName}, I know you've been prejudiced against me ever since that day... but why must you think of me as such a terrible person?
Her meek expression cracks momentarily, but she quickly masks it with a show of panic and hurt. Seeing her still adamantly denying everything, you decide to approach this from a different angle.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: In Désir, you voluntarily took up the role of a mail carrier. Just now, you were happy to be able to deliver mail again. You said it was because that job brings hope to everyone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You didn't hesitate to violate your code of conduct and deliver fake letters in order to protect the townsfolk's feelings. In other words, you're saying you were willing to do something wrong because it was for their own good.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Yes, it pained me to... forge those letters too. If I hadn't seen everyone's smiling faces when delivering the mail, I couldn't have kept going... What's... what's wrong with that?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: No, there's nothing wrong with that.

choices.text: No, there's nothing wrong with that.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Delivering mail does let you get close to the recipients and see their joy firsthand. For you... that meant watching them continue to believe in you and the beautiful dream you'd woven.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But for someone as kind as you, when you saw their smiles from the false hope given by you, did you never once think about what would happen when their dreams finally shattered?
Dove opens her mouth to explain, but after several failed attempts, she falls silent. You seize this moment to elaborate on your theory.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Maybe you never considered the consequences, or you did but chose to ignore them. Either way, that was not the behavior of an honorable messenger who would violate her own principles for the sake of people's trust and happiness.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Which means your true motive for creating and delivering these fake letters is questionable.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: W-what other motive could I have? What could I possibly gain from this?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: True, you might not have gained any material benefits from this. But what if your satisfaction was purely psychological?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: For instance, many compulsive liars simply enjoy the sense of superiority that comes from deceiving others. They revel in watching their victims fall from grace, finding pleasure in their pain and suffering. It makes them laugh with delight.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, is this really how you see me... Why?
Her hurt expression is so innocent, but you remain unmoved.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm simply trying to find a motive that fits your actions. If deceiving people with fake letters wasn't your means to an end, but the end itself, then it explains everything.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Your real motive for becoming a mail carrier was simply this: to deceive the townsfolk with fake letters, reinforce their fantasies, and ensure their suffering would be even greater when the town finally collapsed, all while securing a front-row seat to watch it unfold, wasn't it?
Having laid out your final conclusion, you watch Dove intently, studying every nuance of her expression and reaction.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Even an S-Class Sinner wouldn't have been able to maintain Désir's facade forever. You knew that all along, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But knowing it would all come crashing down, you still delayed people's escape, sabotaged others' efforts, and kept them trapped on a sinking ship.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Pure altruism alone can't explain your contradictory actions, but one mixed with ill intentions can. Unless you have an even deeper, more compelling reason that might convince me?
You deliberately pause here, giving Dove time to think. You are indeed anticipating a better explanation or a more convincing reason she might have to justify her actions.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...Yes, you're right! I forged those letters for my own pleasure. I just loved watching those pathetic weaklings succumb to my lies.
But in the end, all you get is the shattering of her gentle, harmless facade. All her carefully hidden thorns now point directly at you.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Oh, how very smart you are! Yes, your guess is exactly right! You've got your answer! Are you satisfied now? Should I give you a prize, great Chief of the wonderful DisCity?
Her long-suppressed emotions explode in a torrent of bitter mockery. She fixes you with a look both defiant and sneering, having completely abandoned her pretense.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Satisfaction isn't what concerns me. What I want to know is why you did this. What could you gain from it?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Ha! You want to know why I deceived others? Because I was the one who was lied to first! My parents lied to me. They promised they'd come back, but they abandoned me and died delivering mail!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: All that talk about being needed by everyone. They were both liars. They died for nothing! The villagers were all spineless cowards who only wanted to hear good news. No one even cared if anything was real or fake!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: They treated my parents' deaths like some kind of joke. They even kept me in the dark while shamelessly forging letters in my parents' voices, trying to get me to tell them where our money was hidden!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: They destroyed my trust and trampled on my dream. All I did was write a few fake letters to get back at them. Merciful enough, wasn't I?
Like a dam breaking, she pours out all the truths about her past that she had kept hidden. Having nothing left to lose, she admits to all your accusations without further denial.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But from what you're saying, all of this happened before you came to Désir. The townsfolk there had nothing to do with it.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: True, they had nothing to do with it. But they have no one to blame but themselves, for they were as blind as those villagers, failing to see what was right in front of them!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: This is WhiteSands we're talking about. How could they possibly get replies so quickly? And the envelopes and paper always looked the same, arriving perfectly intact! Yet they still bought it. What does that tell you?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: It proves that those people in Désir wanted to be fooled! They were the ones clinging to the lies, refusing to wake up. They didn't care if the letters were real. They just wanted to comfort themselves with falsehood!
A contemptuous smirk curls her lips as her voice grows as cold and heavy as the night of WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: You see? No one cared if the letters were fake. All everyone ever cares about is themselves. It's the same in my hometown, Désir, or anywhere else. So I didn't do anything wrong. What could I possibly have done wrong?
Beneath her cracked facade, you see a shattered core like a burnt-out firepit. It's as cold and lifeless as her voice now.

Others' contempt shattered Dove's fantasy of the messenger's job. She began using fake letters both for revenge and to test people, until each successful deception trapped her deeper in the pessimistic cycle.
Faced with Dove's mocking expression, you find yourself at a loss for words.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, what you've said earlier, about your devotion to being a mail carrier, was that all just a lie too?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: It was real once, but not anymore. I'm not foolish enough to be deceived twice.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you didn't mean it when you said you were willing to take up the job as a mail carrier on bail on the Outland routes?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: What kind of question is that?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Unless I can go back to fooling those gullible idiots with fake letters, I refuse to waste my life like my parents did on such a thankless job!
Dove remains contemptuous, her refusal unwavering. But you've already prepared your next move for exactly this kind of response.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Oh? As it happens, a like-minded merchant has just requested to see you. He wants to use your skills to forge letters and sell them to Outlanders for profit.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Isn't this exactly what you're looking for? In that case, I'll arrange a meeting for you.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...I've been perfectly honest with you, and this is your answer? Aren't you supposed to be the good guy, the hero Chief of DisCity?
Now it's Dove's turn to study you with suspicion, trying to guess your true intentions. But you simply meet her gaze calmly, letting her distrustful eyes pass over you.
Though Dove presents herself as a hopeless nihilist, you know that for a dream to shatter, it must first have existed. Moreover, the way she spoke about her parents shows that she still cares.
Perhaps that shattered dream can still move her. You're not ready to pass your final judgment yet. You hope this merchant might be the fuel needed to reignite the dying embers in her heart.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Hmph, I can't tell what exactly you're up to, but if it involves delivering mail...
She blinks, her suspicious expression vanishing as she puts on her sweet innocent smile once more.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Ahem... then I would be more than happy to help, Chief.
